message.reasoning:
Deciding whether to buy Atlantic Avenue or start an auction.

I own two of three yellows. Buying Atlantic would leave me with $203 cash, but I cannot complete the monopoly since Marvin Gardens is owned by p1.

I am checking pink property rent values. p3 has St. Charles, States, and Virginia at four houses each. I need to verify the exact rent amounts before deciding whether to buy Atlantic Avenue.

Pink property rents are $750–$1,000 at four houses. p4's dark blues at three houses each cost $1,100–$1,400. With only $203 cash after buying Atlantic, I cannot survive either threat. I will not purchase it.

Atlantic Avenue would cost $260 for a base rent of only $22. Its mortgage value is just $130, so buying it would lose $130 in liquidity. I cannot complete the yellow group without trading with p1, who is nearly broke and likely will not sell their blocker.

Building is the win condition. Two houses on the greens would cost $400, leaving only $63 cash. One house each would drain too much cash for the rent increase. I am recalling exact green property rents to confirm.

Mortgaging my other properties to cover the $260 purchase would leave me with only $380 in cash. That is still too risky. I will start an auction instead. Another player might buy it cheaply, or I could win it for less than its full price.

p1 cannot afford to bid. p3 lacks the cash and has no use for Atlantic. p4 has $74 and could buy it for under $130, turning it into a mortgage asset.

Atlantic blocks no one. p1 cannot build a yellow monopoly even with two yellows because they are broke. I would need to trade for Marvin to complete the set, and it is mortgaged.

Owning Atlantic would give me leverage to trade for Marvin later and complete the yellow group. The orange properties are a real threat, but p1 is cash-poor and likely cannot build there. Right now, however, cash is the priority.

Mortgaging all seven properties yields only $1,173 in total liquidity. Boardwalk at three houses costs $1,400, which is impossible to pay even with every mortgage. Park Place at three houses costs $1,100, so it would be barely survivable. I must not reduce cash or liquidity unnecessarily.

Paying $260 for Atlantic Avenue would lower total liquidity from $1,173 to $1,043. That is strictly worse than keeping the cash.

Auctioning it could let me acquire the property for under $130, which would be a clear liquidity win and still give me two yellows. p4 might bid to block me, but they already hold a dark blue monopoly and are building there, so they may not care about denying me another yellow.

p3 is too desperate to bid. They mortgaged everything to pay $600 in Boardwalk rent and need cash for survival.

I could win the auction for as little as $12 to $75. That is well below the $130 mortgage value.

Starting the auction now would decline the direct purchase.

If p4 buys Atlantic cheaply, they cannot complete a yellow set. They also lack unmortgaged properties to mortgage, so they would spend cash on it only for strategic denial. If p1 acquires it, they still cannot build a monopoly without Marvin. Ventnor remains a blocker either way.

Baltic and Oriental are low-value unowned spaces. Oriental would complete the light blue set, but p1 owns Vermont at mortgage and I own Connecticut, so that group is split.

I will start the auction. I am weighing a public message to either bluff that I do not want the property or explain that I am passing to preserve cash for green houses.

I will publicly claim I am passing to save cash, and privately reveal my honest reasoning. This should keep p4 from bidding defensively.

p1 has eight houses on the orange group. I can pay $600 in orange rent with full cash plus mortgages, but that would force me to mortgage greens and break my monopoly. I am now calculating exact orange rent values to confirm the threat.

Exact orange rent values are now confirmed. St. James at two houses costs $200, Tennessee at three houses costs $550, and New York at three houses costs $600. I am currently on Atlantic Avenue and will move from there on the next roll.
